To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we provide a Bifidodobacterium-specific ITS-based profiling pipeline for the precise appraisal of bifidobacteria in the human gut, which can be easily implemented in any microbiology lab.

the internal transcribed spacers (ITS) region of the Bifidoacterium genus can be used to define a primer set that can be used for the precise taxonomic identification at the species level and that this primer set can be used in a targeted amplicons sequencing protocol to evaluate the composition of the Bifodobacterium community in the human gastrointestinal tract.

the Bifidbacterium-specific ITS amplicons can be reliably used for precise bifidobacterial taxonomic identification and that the Bifdobacterium-specific ITS profiling protocol is suitable for the detailed characterization of the bifidibacterial community composition in human gut samples.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the definition of a new molecular marker, namely the ITS, for the precise identification of Bifidobateria and the development of an ITS-based protocol for the analysis of the Bifdobacteria community composition of human gut samples.
the development of a targeted ITS-based protocol for the precise appraisal of the human gut bifidobacterial microbiota.

the definition of a novel amplicon-based approach for precise bifidobacterial profiling, which can be applied in the future to the investigation of the role played by Bifidobacterial species in the human gut microbiome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ITS-based profiling pipeline is a valuable tool that can be used to precisely and reliably characterize the bifidobacterium community in the human gastrointestinal tract.
this work provides a valuable tool for a precise and subspecies-specific reconstruction of the human gut bifidobacterial population.

the BifidusITS protocol represents a powerful approach to investigate the composition of Bifidobacterial communities, providing a valuable tool for a precise and accurate assessment of the bifidibacterial community composition in human gut microbiota samples, as well as in other ecosystems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed an ITS-based amplicon sequencing protocol that allows the precise identification of all currently known bifidobacterial species and subspecies in the human gut microbiome.

the ITS amplicon sequencing approach is an effective tool to assess the bifidobacteriota of human gut samples, and it may be used as a complementary tool to 16S rDNA-based approaches for a more precise and detailed characterization of the human gut bifidobacterial population.
we provide a novel protocol to evaluate the composition of the bifidbacterial community in human gut by means a targeted amplicons sequencing approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ITS-based profiling approach is able to accurately reconstruct the bifidobacteria composition of the human intestinal ecosystem, thus providing a useful tool to investigate the role of this bacterial group in human health and disease.
the use of the ITS as target for Bifidobacterial profiling is superior to the use of 165 rRNA gene variable region-based approaches.
the application of ITS amplicon sequencing represents a valid and reliable alternative to the use of 165 rRNA gene amplicon sequencing to assess the composition of the gut Bifidobacterial community.
